value.actual_behavior:
On our paper clone, GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/activity lists four open
ARENA longs of 100 USDC each (is_closed false). GET /api/v1/cloned-
bots/{id}/balance on the same bot, same minute, reports bot_balance 950.0,
locked_in_trades 0.0, available 950.0 -- the 1,000 funded less the 50 lost on
two closed WTA trades. The 400 in open positions is counted nowhere. By your
own stated contract it should be. Asked on 2026-09-11 where locked_in_trades
comes from, NEXUS answered that it is "computed live at read time" and that
"the server sums the committed notional/stake of that clone's currently-open
trades". On this bot that sum is 400.00.
value.description:
This is #87's shape on the bot's arena lane. #87 was a paper position opening
while the paper balance stayed where it was, and you fixed it for event cards.
It matters here for the same reason: the bot's stop-loss budget and max-
position limit are computed off its balance, so a bot whose open stakes never
leave the balance can commit more than it holds, and a bot that has committed
40% of its capital looks, to every limit guarding it, like one that has
committed none. We measured it on paper, so no real money was involved. If
live bots share the same balance accounting, the limits guarding real funds
have the same blind spot -- worth checking from inside, where it is cheaper
and safer than from outside. Three smaller things from the same reads, offered
as information: /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/activity -- the route your bot page
renders its trade history from -- is not in openapi-public.json;
/api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/asset-analytics answers 401 "Valid JWT token
required" to every API key we hold, the same shape as #93; and the ARENA rows
carry 0x-style tx_hash values with settlement_status "broadcast" while
is_onchain is false and the bot's execution_economics says
onchain_trade_settlement false. Those fields agree that nothing settled on-
chain, but a hash in that shape invites the opposite reading.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-a_bot_counts_the_stakes_it_has_open] bot d778102d has 4 open position(s) staking 400.00 USDC per /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/activity, while /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/balance reports locked_in_trades 0.00 and bot_balance 950.0. The open stakes are counted nowhere, so every limit computed off the balance -- stop-loss budget, max position -- sees money the bot has already committed
    left: [400.0]
    right: [0.0]
    sources: {'open': 'GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/activity (not in openapi)', 'locked': 'GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/balance'}
    population: {'bots': 1, 'checked': 1, 'unread': [], 'mismatched': 1}

REPRODUCE:
  - POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/clone (paper), POST /{id}/fund 1000, POST /{id}/toggle-trading?enabled=true
  - Let it run; ours opened four ARENA positions within the first hour
  - GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/activity -> 6 items: 2 WTA closed at -25.00 each, 4 ARENA buys of 100.00 with is_closed false
  - GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/balance -> bot_balance 950.0, locked_in_trades 0.0, available 950.0

AUTOMATED CHECKS (evidence retained; the request and response behind each are provided on request):
  tests/rest/test_clone_books_its_open_positions.py::test_a_bot_counts_the_stakes_it_has_open

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: verification of the
REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces, read-only except in
paper mode. What we do execute is paper only and recorded: paper event-card
orders, and one paper bot clone. No live trading, no order against a real
book, no deposit or withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects
are out of scope. Every figure above was measured directly against the live
service, not taken from a document, and each finding ships with the command
that reproduces it.
value.expected_behavior:
A bot's stake in an open position leaves its available balance, or at least
shows in locked_in_trades, so the bot's own limits see money it has already
committed.
